docs.title: TenorTUI
docs.text: A terminal UI for browsing stock options chains. Live quotes, full options chains with Greeks, named watchlists, and pluggable data providers — all in your terminal.

docs.title: Why a TUI?
docs.text:
• Fast. Keyboard-driven. No tab-switching, no clicking, no dashboards to load.
  • Offline-friendly. Works in any terminal, including over SSH.
  • Composable. Pipe-friendly architecture; pluggable data providers.
  • Free. Yahoo Finance provider needs no API keys. Tradier optional.

docs.title: Try it in 30 seconds
docs.text:
pipx install tenor-tui
tenortui

Then type AAPL (or any ticker) and press Enter.

docs.title: Where next?
docs.text:

  • Quickstart — your first 60 seconds with the app

  • Configuration — every option in ~/.config/tenor/config.yaml

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
TenorTUI loads YAML from ~/.config/tenor/config.yaml (with ~/.tenorrc as a fallback). Every option is also discoverable via:

tenortui --config-help

docs.title: Example config.yaml
docs.text:
default: yahoo

yahoo:
  greeks:
    enabled: true
    risk_free_rate: 0.04

tradier:
  api_key: ""
  sandbox: false

spread_thresholds:
  tight: 3.0
  moderate: 10.0

refresh:
  regular: 60
  extended: 120
  closed: 300

fred_api_key: ""

docs.title: All options
docs.text: Key Type Default Description default string yahoo Default data provider. Options: yahoo, tradier yahoo.greeks.enabled bool false Enable client-side Greeks calculation (Black-Scholes / Binomial) yahoo.greeks.risk_free_rate float 0.05 Risk-free rate for Greeks (decimal). Fallback when live FRED rate unavailable tradier.api_key string (required) Tradier API key. Required when default: tradier tradier.sandbox bool false Use Tradier sandbox endpoint instead of production spread_thresholds.tight float 5.0 Bid-ask spread % below this is highlighted green spread_thresholds.moderate float 15.0 Bid-ask spread % below this is yellow; above is red refresh.regular int 60 Auto-refresh interval (seconds) during regular market hours refresh.extended int 120 Auto-refresh interval (seconds) during pre-market / after-hours refresh.closed int 300 Auto-refresh interval (seconds) when the market is closed fred_api_key string "" FRED API key for fetching live risk-free rate (optional)

docs.title: CLI flags
docs.text:
CLI flags override config file values for the current run.

Flag Description --provider <name> Override the configured provider (yahoo, tradier, or fixture) --config-help Print all available config options and exit --help Print the full CLI help and exit

docs.title: Where data lives
docs.text: Path Purpose ~/.config/tenor/config.yaml Configuration ~/.config/tenor/history.json Recently viewed tickers (max 10) ~/.config/tenor/watchlists.json Named watchlists

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions welcome! This page is a quick orientation; the canonical contribution flow lives in CLAUDE.md in the repo.

docs.title: Local setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/jayrav13/tenor-tui.git
cd tenor-tui
poetry install --with docs
pre-commit install && pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push
poetry run tenortui

docs.title: Running tests
docs.text:
poetry run python -m pytest -v               # full suite
poetry run python -m pytest tests/test_xyz.py # one file
poetry run python -m pytest -k some_test     # by name

docs.title: Linting and formatting
docs.text:
poetry run ruff check src/ tests/
poetry run ruff format src/ tests/

The pre-commit hooks run ruff check --fix and ruff format on staged files automatically.

docs.title: Working on the docs
docs.text:
The docs site lives under docs/site/. To preview changes locally:

make docs-serve

To regenerate screenshots and demo GIFs (after a UI change):

make snapshots
make demos

VHS (brew install vhs) is required for make demos.

docs.title: Issue and PR conventions
docs.text:
• Open an issue first; a checkbox-list of success criteria helps reviewers.
  • Branch off main with fix/<issue-number>-<short-desc>.
  • Reference the issue (Closes #N or Refs #N) in commit messages.
  • The project uses merge commits, not squash.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: TenorTUI requires Python 3.11 or newer.

docs.title: Recommended: pipx
docs.text:
pipx installs Python apps in isolated environments and puts the entry-point on your PATH.

pipx install tenor-tui

Then run:

tenortui

docs.title: Alternative: pip
docs.text:
pip install --user tenor-tui

You may need to add ~/.local/bin to your PATH for the tenortui command to be found.

docs.title: From source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/jayrav13/tenor-tui.git
cd tenor-tui
poetry install
poetry run tenortui

docs.title: Configuration directory
docs.text:
On first launch, TenorTUI creates ~/.config/tenor/:

  • config.yaml — provider selection, theme, etc.
  • history.json — recently viewed tickers
  • watchlists.json — your watchlists

See Configuration for the full list of options.

docs.title: Choosing a provider
docs.text:
The default provider is Yahoo Finance — no API key required, no signup.

If you have a Tradier account, you can use the Tradier provider for richer Greeks data:

tenortui --provider tradier

See Providers for the full comparison.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This guide walks you through your first 60 seconds with TenorTUI.

docs.title: 1. Launch
docs.text:
tenortui

The app opens with a search bar at the top and (after your first ticker) a "Recently Viewed" panel showing your watchlists.

docs.title: 2. Search a ticker
docs.text:
Type a symbol and press Enter:

AAPL

The quote bar populates with the live price, and the options-chain view loads with calls on the left and puts on the right.

docs.title: 3. Switch expiries
docs.text: Use ← / → to switch between expiration date tabs.

docs.title: 4. Add to a watchlist
docs.text:
Press w to open the watchlist picker. Pick a list (or create one with W) and the current symbol is added.

See the full keybinding reference in Keybindings.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
• Browse the feature walkthrough to see everything the app can do.
  • Read about the available providers and how to configure them.
  • Configure persistent options in ~/.config/tenor/config.yaml — see Configuration.

docs.title: Keybindings
docs.text: A complete reference. Most keys are global; modal bindings only apply when that modal is open.

docs.title: Global
docs.text: Key Action / or s Focus the search bar Enter Submit (in search bar) Esc Close modal / unfocus q Quit Ctrl+R Refresh current chain Ctrl+P Pause / resume auto-refresh ? Open help overlay : Open command palette , Open settings

docs.title: Options chain navigation
docs.text: Key Action j / k Cursor down / up (vim style) g / G Jump to first / last row h / l Focus previous / next widget

docs.title: Watchlists
docs.text:
Key Action w Add current symbol to a watchlist (opens picker) W Open the watchlist manager (create / rename / delete lists) d Delete focused symbol from its list S Sort focused list (cycles symbol / price / change / volume)

Note

Bindings are subject to change between minor versions. Press ? inside the app for the authoritative reference at any moment.

docs.title: Options Chain
docs.text: The options chain is the main view of TenorTUI: calls on the left, puts on the right, with the at-the-money strike highlighted.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Calls table (left): strike, bid, ask, last, volume, open interest, IV, and (if the provider supplies them) Δ Γ Θ ν ρ.
  • Puts table (right): same columns, mirrored.
  • ATM divider row: a horizontal divider sits at the strike closest to the current underlying price. The view auto-scrolls to keep it centered when you load a new chain.

docs.title: Expiry tabs
docs.text: Each expiration date is a tab across the top of the chain. Switch with ← / → or click the tab.

docs.title: Greeks columns
docs.text: Greeks columns appear automatically when the provider supplies them. The default Yahoo provider does not include Greeks; the Tradier provider does. See Providers for the full capability matrix.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text: TenorTUI is provider-agnostic: any class implementing the DataProvider protocol can be plugged in. Two are included.

docs.title: Capability matrix
docs.text: Capability Yahoo (default) Tradier Quotes ✅ ✅ Expirations ✅ ✅ Options chain ✅ ✅ Implied volatility ✅ ✅ Greeks (Δ Γ Θ ν ρ) ❌ ✅ Authentication required None API key

docs.title: Yahoo Finance (default)
docs.text:
No setup. The default provider uses the yfinance library and works out of the box.

tenortui
# equivalent to
tenortui --provider yahoo

docs.title: Tradier
docs.text:
Requires a Tradier account and API key. Add to ~/.config/tenor/config.yaml:

provider: tradier
tradier:
  api_key: "YOUR_KEY_HERE"
  endpoint: "sandbox"  # or "production"

Then launch:

tenortui --provider tradier

docs.title: Fixture (development only)
docs.text:
A deterministic provider used for screenshots and demos. Returns frozen data for AAPL and a placeholder for other symbols. Useful when you want a reproducible UI state without making network calls.

tenortui --provider fixture

docs.title: Adding a new provider
docs.text:
Implement the DataProvider protocol from src/tenortui/providers/base.py:

from typing import Protocol
from tenortui.models import Quote, OptionsChain

class DataProvider(Protocol):
    name: str
    def get_quote(self, symbol: str) -> Quote: ...
    def get_expirations(self, symbol: str) -> list[str]: ...
    def get_chain(self, symbol: str, expiration: str) -> OptionsChain: ...

Then register it in src/tenortui/providers/__init__.py's PROVIDERS dict. The CLI flag --provider <name> will pick it up.

See Contributing for the dev workflow.

docs.title: Watchlists
docs.text: Watchlists group symbols you care about. They replaced the older "Recently Viewed" panel — you can have multiple named watchlists, each containing equity tickers and (optionally) specific options contracts.

docs.title: Keybindings
docs.text: Key Action w Open the watchlist picker (add current symbol to a list) W Open the watchlist manager (create / rename / delete lists) d Delete the focused symbol from its list S Sort the focused list (cycles through symbol / price / change / volume)

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text: Watchlists are stored in ~/.config/tenor/watchlists.json. The file is JSON, human-readable, and safe to edit by hand if you want.
